# Bugs — `arch::x86::mem::paging::table`

No code bugs were found in this module. All scope functions admit correct
specs as written; the only obstacles are a Verus language limitation and a
deferred abstraction, both recorded below for the proving phase.

## Not a code bug — Verus limitation (int-to-ptr cast)

`Table::read` / `Table::write` materialize a raw pointer from the integer base
address (`usize as *const/*mut PteWord`) and perform a volatile access of
externally-owned page-table memory. Verus does not support `usize`→pointer
casts (`error: Verus does not support this cast: usize to *const u32`). This is
a tooling limitation, not a logic error in the code. Mitigated with the
documented `external_body` trust boundary (see `verus-unsupported.md` and
`verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`). No fix required.

## Resolved (Turn 1 review) — read/write now carry full contracts

The earlier "deferred round-trip / addr-only View" note was resolved during the
Turn 1 specification review. `read`/`write` and the `TableEntry` codec now carry
complete `#[verus_spec]` contracts referencing a **global, parameter-free**
page-table-memory ghost (`spec_table_word`/`spec_table_read`), mirroring
`frame::instance`→`phys_view()`. No exec signature changed, so the out-of-scope
`admit()` callers do not cascade (`make verify`: kernel 76 verified, 0 errors).
The `entries: Map<nat, Option<E>>` model and the read-after-write round-trip law
(`lemma_entry_roundtrip`) are now expressed, not deferred. `read`/`write` remain
`external_body` only for the genuine Verus `usize`→pointer limitation below.

165.     /// # Description
166.     ///
167.     /// Creates a table reference from a base address.
168.     ///
169.     /// # Safety
170.     ///
171.     /// `base` must be a valid, page-aligned address with at least one page of readable/writable
172.     /// memory.
173.     ///

175.         ensures result@.addr == base as nat,

185.     /// # Description

187.     /// Reads the entry at `index`.
188.     ///

190.     ///
191.     /// # Safety

204.         requires
205.             index@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
206.         ensures

208.     )]

211.         let ptr: *const PteWord = (self.base + offset) as *const PteWord;

213.     }

218.     /// Writes `entry` at `index`.

223.     ///

243.         requires
244.             index@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
245.     )]

1. verus! {
2. 
3. //==================================================================================================
4. // TableIndex — a validated page-table slot number
5. //==================================================================================================
6. 
7. // A `TableIndex` carries exactly one piece of caller-visible information: the validated index
8. // value. Its abstract value is a single `nat` (see `view_design.md`).
9. impl View for TableIndex {
10.     type V = nat;
11. 
12.     // `closed`: callers reference `self@` and the in-range invariant; the mapping to the inner
13.     // `usize` field is hidden. The abstract value is "the validated slot number".
14.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> nat {
15.         self.0 as nat
16.     }
17. }
18. 
19. impl TableIndex {
20.     // The validated-range guarantee every caller depends on: a `TableIndex` is always a legal
21.     // slot. Enforced as a type invariant so the bound holds unconditionally for any value callers
22.     // hold — this is exactly what keeps `read`/`write` (and `gva.rs`'s `checked_mul`) within one
23.     // page, and is established once at each construction site (`new`, `pd_index`, `pt_index`).
24.     #[verifier::type_invariant]
25.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
26.         self@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH
27.     }
28. }
29. 
30. //==================================================================================================
31. // Virtual-address index extraction (pure helpers)
32. //==================================================================================================
33. 
34. // Low `log2(PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH)` bits of `vaddr >> shift`. Mirrors the exec masking
35. // `(vaddr >> shift) & (PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1)` exactly; the mask makes the result `< LEN`.
36. pub open spec fn spec_table_index(vaddr: usize, shift: usize) -> nat {
37.     ((vaddr >> shift) & ((crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH - 1) as usize)) as nat
38. }
39. 
40. // PD index = bits [PGTAB_SHIFT, PGTAB_SHIFT + log2(LEN)) of `vaddr`.
41. pub open spec fn spec_pd_index(vaddr: usize) -> nat {
42.     spec_table_index(vaddr, crate::mem::PGTAB_SHIFT)
43. }
44. 
45. // PT index = bits [PAGE_SHIFT, PAGE_SHIFT + log2(LEN)) of `vaddr`.
46. pub open spec fn spec_pt_index(vaddr: usize) -> nat {
47.     spec_table_index(vaddr, crate::mem::PAGE_SHIFT)
48. }
49. 
50. //==================================================================================================
51. // TableEntry codec (the per-entry round-trip law)
52. //==================================================================================================
53. 
54. // Abstract serialization / decoding of a `TableEntry`. These mirror the exec `raw` / `from_raw`
55. // trait methods. They are deliberately *unbounded* over `E` (no `TableEntry` bound) to avoid a
56. // definitional cycle (`TableEntry`'s method specs reference these, so a bound here would make the
57. // trait depend on a function that depends on the trait).
58. //
59. // `spec_entry_from_raw` returns `None` for a word that is not a valid encoding of `E` — exactly
60. // the `read` failure path callers map to `InvalidArgument` (see `caller_analysis.md`).
61. pub uninterp spec fn spec_entry_raw<E>(e: E) -> PteWord;
62. 
63. pub uninterp spec fn spec_entry_from_raw<E>(w: PteWord) -> Option<E>;
64. 
65. //==================================================================================================
66. // Global ghost model of page-table memory
67. //==================================================================================================
68. 
69. // Page-table memory is volatile, caller-owned storage the `Table<E>` handle does not contain
70. // (the struct holds only `base`). It is modeled here as a *global, parameter-free* ghost
71. // function — the same device used for the physical-frame subsystem (`mm::phys::phys_view()`):
72. // the abstract state is named globally rather than threaded through a permission parameter, so
73. // `read`/`write` keep their exec signatures and do not cascade ghost arguments into out-of-scope
74. // callers (`identity_map::ensure_pt`/`ensure_pte`/`identity_map_page`).
75. //
76. // `spec_table_word(addr, index)` is the raw word currently stored at slot `index` of the
77. // page-table page based at `addr`. Because it is a pure function, a call to `write` only updates
78. // knowledge about the *one* slot named in its `ensures`; every other slot/page is automatically
79. // preserved across the call (the caller-facing frame condition). The cross-call write transition
80. // (and its consistency when the same slot is written twice) is realized in the proving phase by a
81. // ghost token over the page-table pages — exactly the `phys_view()` "transition realized in the
82. // proving phase" placeholder.
83. pub uninterp spec fn spec_table_word(addr: nat, index: nat) -> PteWord;
84. 
85. // The decoded entry currently stored at slot `index` of the page based at `addr`: the value a
86. // `read` returns. This is the `index -> Option<E>` entry map from `view_design.md`, expressed
87. // pointwise over the global word store.
88. pub open spec fn spec_table_read<E>(addr: nat, index: nat) -> Option<E> {
89.     spec_entry_from_raw::<E>(spec_table_word(addr, index))
90. }
91. 
92. //==================================================================================================
93. // Table<E> — a typed, non-owning handle over one page-table page
94. //==================================================================================================
95. 
96. // To callers a `Table<E>` is a typed handle over the page at a physical/identity-mapped base
97. // address (see `view_design.md`): its caller-meaningful identity is *which page* read/write act
98. // on (`addr`), and its observable contents are the per-slot decoded entry map (`entries`). The
99. // contents live in volatile, caller-owned memory the struct does not store, so the view reads
100. // them from the global `spec_table_read` ghost rather than from struct fields.
101. pub struct TableView<E> {
102.     /// Physical/identity-mapped base address this handle denotes.
103.     pub addr: nat,
104.     /// Decoded entry at each valid slot — `entries[i]` is what `read(i)` returns
105.     /// (`None` = the slot holds a word that is not a valid encoding of `E`).
106.     pub entries: Map<nat, Option<E>>,
107. }
108. 
109. impl<E: TableEntry> View for Table<E> {
110.     type V = TableView<E>;
111. 
112.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> TableView<E> {
113.         TableView {
114.             addr: self.base as nat,
115.             entries: Map::new(
116.                 |i: nat| i < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
117.                 |i: nat| spec_table_read::<E>(self.base as nat, i),
118.             ),
119.         }
120.     }
121. }
122. 
123. } // verus!
